title: Advertising: An Industry

Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: State true or false about guidelines for advertising: (i) Ads cannot contain any exaggerated, exceptional or misleading claim. (ii) Women can be portrayed as passive, weak or submissive in advertisements.
State true or false: (i) Advertising is a paid form of communication. (ii) PR is subtle and indirect.

Match: (i) Creative director (ii) Copy writer with (a) supervises the production of the advertisements (b) produces the wording of an advertisement; and (iii) Visualizer with (c) creates images for the advertisements.
Fill in the blanks: A ______ is an advertisement on audio or visual mediums; a ______ is a rhyming song used to advertise a product.
State true or false: (i) Ads can be presented as news. (ii) Ads cannot insult any race or caste.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is the importance of market research and media planning in agencies?
questions.answer: Market research gathers data on customers' likes to plan campaigns and products; media planning allocates the budget and selects the media, size and frequency of the ad.

questions.q: Name any two units that work under the creative department in an ad agency.
questions.answer: Copywriting and visualizing (the creative director supervises them).

questions.q: List any two functions of a Media Planner in an ad agency.
questions.answer: Prepares and allocates the advertising budget; selects the media and decides the frequency, size and position of the ad.

questions.q: What is a freelancer in advertising?
questions.answer: A person who works independently with no long-term contract, paid according to the work done.

questions.q: What is meant by market research?
questions.answer: The systematic gathering, recording and analysing of data about customers to decide products, ads and markets.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: List three advertising principles and briefly describe them with examples.
questions.answer: Gain attention (size, colour, slogan); stimulate desire (make the product seem special or cool); impart conviction (show certainty, e.g. a fairness cream promising success).

questions.q: Explain the key points to be kept in mind while planning an ad campaign.
questions.answer: Why advertise, target group, message, location of the target group and medium, length of the ad and campaign, language and visuals.

questions.q: Describe any three guidelines governing advertising.
questions.answer: No exaggerated or misleading claims; no direct endorsement of tobacco or liquor; no portrayal of women as passive or submissive.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Discuss four important ethical guidelines to consider while producing an advertisement.
questions.answer: Ads must not mislead or exaggerate; must not offend morality, decency, religion, caste or race; must not provoke violence or portray women as weak; tobacco, liquor and medicinal products need special care and approval.

questions.q: Differentiate between advertisements and public relations. Give examples.
questions.answer: Advertisement is paid, direct and explicit and reveals the sponsor (a soap ad); PR is not directly paid, is subtle and indirect and may not reveal who is behind it (a community service campaign).

questions.q: Describe the structure and functions of an ad agency.
questions.answer: Owner or president, creative director, copywriter, visualizer, media planner, market research team and production in-charge; freelancers also work in the agency.
